Subfactors, index and finite-depth classification

Finite completion with separate tunnel cells

An exact finite partition may use a different tunnel on each supported cell. This makes finite positive sums of projection traces the right certificates for completing a residual while retaining the selected old blocks. We prove that criterion, then relate the central capacity cost to the ordered overlap of finite-stage representatives. These are two sufficient construction routes; the unrestricted amenability input remains to be proved.

The original finite full-partition statement

Popa's Theorem 4.4.1(1), printed p.222, concerns finite-index inclusions of II₁ factors. The hypothesis is that is an amenable inclusion; part (1) additionally assumes . For every and finite , it asserts finite-dimensional unital , , with

and a finite set , an actual tunnel for each , and projections

The source permits different continuations and different finite lengths. Orthogonality follows from the projection sum: , a sum of positive operators, so . No separability, finite depth, extremality, ergodic core or unique norm trace is imposed in part (1). Those hypotheses belong to other statements and are not inserted here. Taking adjoints of (FP.0) gives .

The source's proof refers to the preceding maximality argument and reduced-algebra heredity. That preceding ergodic-core amalgamation, printed pp.220–221, starts with supports in tail factors. The whole-stage supports of 76.2 instead lie in finite smaller relative commutants. Replacing one membership by the other is not a justified replay of that amalgamation.

Exact human source: Sorin Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II, Acta Mathematica 172 (1994), 163–255, DOI, 4.1.1–4.1.2, printed pp.209–210, and 4.4, printed pp.220–222.

Lemma FP.3 — the exact trace-fiber test and a sufficient order test. The following are equivalent:

In particular, it is sufficient that, at some fixed finite level, a trace-zero kernel correction makes every compatible norm trace strictly positive on . For , the sufficient condition is simply for every . No upper bound is needed.

Proof. If a positive integer vector at any finite level represents , move it and to a common later level and take . Trace compatibility gives . Conversely the vector is exactly a positive certificate in FP.2. This proves the equivalence.

For the sufficient test apply the minimum half of 79.2, the finite order test. At the fixed starting level, for ,

The trace space is compact by 79.1 and evaluation is continuous. Strict positivity at every trace therefore gives a strictly positive attained minimum. At a sufficiently late finite stage all the promoted coordinates are nonnegative integers. Their ambient trace is still ; apply FP.1 and FP.2. Unlike a single unit-capacity projection certificate, multiple cells do not require these coordinates to be at most . The trace-zero correction can be nonzero even if the originally chosen vector fails order tests. Conversely positive ambient trace alone does not supply a kernel correction or norm-trace positivity. This is the precise arithmetic step still to be derived from actual amenable-inclusion data if one pursues an unchanged-family completion.

Exact remaining obligation

FP.2 improves the current residual route in an essential way: the printed endpoint requires a finite positive sum of finite traces, not necessarily a single finite projection of the residual trace. FP.9 is the exact finite-support realization obstruction for a completion that keeps the chosen old blocks unchanged. FP.12–FP.16 give a different quantitative sufficient route that permits small cuts.

The original unrestricted theorem would follow from a construction, for each target family and tolerance, of a 76.4-type selected family whose residual lies in , or of a family satisfying the small-cut certificate, or from another complete argument producing FP.1 directly. The arguments here do not prove that arbitrary amenability supplies any of these alternatives. A negative coordinate of one signed representative, a positive central cost for one fixed family, or an abstract trace diagnostic is not an actual counterexample to Popa 4.4.1(1). No change in its original hypotheses or finite full-support conclusion is made.

Common ordinary stage, retained higher prefix, nested approximations, generating tunnels, the second central local form, unrestricted common-support BF and represented/opposite models remain separate original mathematical obligations. The above-four operator projection expectation identity is also a separate input; no implication from general amenability to that identity is used.

Exercise FP.1 — one residual cell or finitely many? In the abstract algebra , give the three minimal projections the inherited weights . List its projection trace set. In the ambient factor split the physical into two orthogonal projections of trace . Their sum is by faithfulness. Each is unitarily conjugate in that factor to the first minimal projection.

The three old canonical supports have rank sum , while the identity ranks are . Thus and . Put . Then

The first coordinate of exceeds the unit capacity one. Its two bounded pieces supply the finite multi-cell certificate; demanding would lose that route. The second and third characters of evaluate at zero, so the strict all-trace positivity test is not necessary for this exact positive certificate. The first character evaluates it at two, explaining why an upper all-trace bound below one is not part of the multi-cell criterion.

These are finite-algebra and factor-comparison calculations. They do not identify with an actual smaller Jones relative commutant, prove amenability of an inclusion, or produce its full larger row. To invoke Theorem FP.2 one must supply the actual finite whole-tunnel pairs and their inherited weights, the old selected square, and the actual finite-alignment/exact-placement inputs. With those hypotheses, each new physical cell can use its own actual continuation and the theorem gives both expectation identities and preserves the old target errors. No Jones realization or counterexample is inferred from this numerical example.

Exercise FP.2 — check the two sufficient certificates. Let an actual selected square and its canonical finite-stage data have all the hypotheses of FP.2–FP.5.

(a) At some level suppose is an integer vector with , , and for every compatible norm tracial state. Explain how the one-sided order test yields finitely many residual cells. Must every be below one?

(b) Independently, suppose a finite stage has , , and a proposed rotated family has ordered overlap . Suppose the target norms are at most one and the original target errors are strictly below . Verify the overlap/cut inequalities and the strict certificate for final tolerance . Give an explicit final error bound and describe which physical supports may change.

(c) Explain why neither part proves that general amenability supplies its assumed certificate.

Solution. For (a), the minimum limit (FP.10) is at least . Choose a finite later level with . Every coordinate of is then positive; it remains an integer vector and its actual ambient trace remains . If some coordinates exceed their block sizes, apply the explicit finite decomposition (FP.3). Each piece has bounded valid ranks, and the sum of its traces is exactly . Theorem FP.2 places the corresponding finitely many orthogonal physical residual cells separately. No upper all-trace bound is required: the certificate is a finite sum, not a single unit-capacity projection. Compactness and the stated uniform positivity justify the finite choice; positive ambient trace alone would not justify it.

For (b), the minimum is at most the proposed . The lower bound applies to every proposed rotated family, while the upper bound constructs a possibly different family. The supplied numbers are consistent with

The last inequality here is strict, illustrating why the proof says that the constructed family satisfies the upper bound rather than always attaining equality. With , the required threshold is

Indeed , and , so the strict threshold holds. By , the extra target error is at most

Together with the original strict error below , the final error is strictly below . The sharper bound using the given capacity is , but the overlap certificate already suffices. Optimal physical cuts remove total trace from the old supports. Their remainder is enlarged by that exact amount, and the finite canonical complement supplies its trace certificate. A cut old support can change or disappear; zero cells are omitted. Every resulting cell has a full actual whole-tunnel pair and their sum is exactly one. Both expectation orders hold. The targets remain fixed; no earlier ordinary-prefix retention is asserted.

For (c), part (a) assumes a particular actual kernel correction and positivity on every compatible norm trace. Part (b) assumes a particular actual finite selection with verified small overlap and capacity. The proofs convert those data into finite exact partitions; they do not derive either dataset from unrestricted amenability. Supplying such data for every target family and tolerance, or constructing the original partition by another complete argument, is the residual input of (FP.0)–(FP.1).
